summary:
Problem: During large forest fires, smoke and clouds block optical satellites, so emergency teams struggle to see where fires have spread and what is damaged.

Our solution: An interactive web app for tracking wildfire surface change. Users pick an event (Marmaris, Manavgat, Bodrum–Milas, 2021) or any two dates and swipe between a “before” and “after” view using NASA GIBS (VIIRS) imagery. The app overlays NASA fire detections, includes an experimental change-detection layer that highlights areas that became darker, and lets users share a link to any view. It also presents Sentinel-1 radar and thermal fire imagery and explains why radar can observe the surface through smoke, cloud and darkness.

Current limits: The live map uses optical NASA imagery as a stand-in. NISAR radar data is not yet integrated, and the change layer is a rough brightness-based indicator.

Next step: Add NISAR L-band data from ASF DAAC, compute radar backscatter change between pre-fire and post-fire dates, and replace the optical layers with the radar change map so fires can be assessed even under smoke.

Impact: Helps firefighters and disaster agencies such as AFAD understand damage faster, without waiting for smoke to clear.
details:
Problem: During large forest fires, thick smoke and clouds block optical satellites, so emergency teams struggle to see where a fire has spread and what has been damaged.

Our solution: “Seeing Through the Smoke” is an interactive web app for tracking wildfire surface change. Users pick a fire (Marmaris, Manavgat or Bodrum–Milas, 2021) or any two dates, and swipe between a “before” and “after” view built from NASA GIBS (VIIRS) satellite imagery. The app overlays NASA fire detections, includes an experimental change-detection layer that highlights areas that became darker, and lets users share a link to any view. It also shows Sentinel-1 radar and thermal fire imagery and explains why radar (SAR) can observe the surface through smoke, cloud and darkness.

Current limits: The live map uses optical NASA imagery as a stand-in. NISAR radar data is not yet integrated, and the change layer is only a rough brightness-based indicator.

Next step: Add NISAR L-band data from ASF DAAC, compute radar backscatter change between pre-fire and post-fire dates, and replace the optical layers with the radar change map, so damage can be assessed even under smoke.

Impact: Helps firefighters and agencies such as AFAD understand damage faster, without waiting for the smoke to clear.

Tools: NASA GIBS (VIIRS true color and fire detections), Sentinel-1, Leaflet, JavaScript.
